newsitem.title: USA: Procter & Gamble posts record profit despite lower sales.
newsitem.headline: Procter & Gamble posts record profit despite lower sales.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co. said Thursday its profits rose by 9 percent to a record $979 million in the latest quarter despite a decline in worldwide sales.
The giant consumer products company said net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 rose to $979 million, or $1.39 a share, from $896 million or $1.27 per share.
The per-share earnings for the company's fiscal first quarter were two cents better than Wall Street estimates of $1.37, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Still, investors sent the Cincinnati-based company's stock reeling. P&G fell $4.25 to $92 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was one of the most active issues.

Procter & Gamble said despite record unit sales volume worldwide, its sales for the quarter slipped to $8.90 billion from $9.03 billion, primarily because of the strong dollar compared with other currencies.
Excluding the effect of unfavourable exchange rates, particularly in Japan and Germany, sales increased consistent with unit volume growth, the company said.

The company, whose brands range from Tide detergent to Pampers diapers and Hawaiian Punch drinks, said its North America shipments, led by the laundry and cleaning products, expanded by 2 percent to a new record as dollar sales rose 1 percent.
P&G said sales and volume increased despite capacity constraints on some fast-growing categories, such as tissues and towels.
The company said unit sales volume in Europe, Middle East and Africa grew 5 percent to a record, but unit volumes were down 9 percent in Asia and 6 percent in Latin America.
